global_organization_chain: Name the job and concede the difficulty.
Credit the individual-level models and say why a whole-building view is needed.
Build the speed from density, first borrowed, then derived.
Reduce the building to one source and one sink.
Recompute the maximum flow at every time step.
Show the bottlenecks on a synthetic building, then run the real one.

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Job, concession, three parts, numbers last.
moves: input: the evacuation task
rhetorical job: name the job and concede the difficulty before the method
analytical job: collapse the individual effect into speed and the building into one source and one sink
output: two run times and one evacuation time
handoff: the three parts are opened in order
input: the growth of concern about safe evacuation
rhetorical job: credit two models and then outgrow them
analytical job: separate the individual scale from the building scale
output: a four-step program
handoff: the first step opens the speed model

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Two causes, one challenge, stated objectives, then implied ones.
moves: input: the visitor mix and the building
rhetorical job: make the challenge earn the deliverable
analytical job: separate stated objectives from inferred ones
output: a numbered objective list
handoff: the objectives set what the results must show

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Bare assumptions, then a short table with a deferral.
moves: input: the modelling choices
rhetorical job: list assumptions without promising reasons
analytical job: fix the symbols the speed laws use
output: five assumptions and a symbol table
handoff: the symbols feed both speed models
input: the speed-density literature
rhetorical job: close each model on the case it fails
analytical job: derive a crowded-channel speed and assemble the four matrices
output: two speeds and one overall matrix
handoff: the matrix is what the algorithm reads

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Rename the goal, cite the theorem, decline the proof, name the change.
moves: input: the overall matrix
rhetorical job: state the equivalence and decline the proof openly
analytical job: wrap Ford-Fulkerson in a time loop that updates density
output: a flow matrix and a margin matrix per step
handoff: the margin locates the bottlenecks

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Classify, then one case each, then the real building.
moves: input: the synthetic graph and the Louvre plan
rhetorical job: count and name the bottleneck classes before treating them
analytical job: compare inlet sums with outlet capacity and read the exit-flow curve
output: a 43.2 second test clearance and a 288.7 second Louvre clearance
handoff: the staged conclusions become the staff advice

section_progressions.positive_pattern: One error size, curves overlap, hedge kept.
moves: input: a five percent density error
rhetorical job: read the figure as a guarantee and keep the hedge
analytical job: compare the perturbed curves with the base
output: overlap until the final drop
handoff: the detector accuracy becomes a recommendation

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Claim with because, then the requirement restated as a limit.
moves: input: the finished model
rhetorical job: pair each strength with its reason
analytical job: separate what travels from what the sensors must supply
output: generalization claim and the sensor limit
handoff: the limit bounds the advice

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Advice addressed to the staff as six steps.
moves: input: the results and the bottlenecks
rhetorical job: frame the advice as a method the user can follow
analytical job: tie each step to a result
output: six instructions
handoff: the instructions close the task

section_progressions.positive_pattern: Name the failure, then judge it unlikely.
moves: input: the known non-termination of the base method
rhetorical job: state the failure before dismissing it
analytical job: bound the chance for this use and bound the storage
output: a judgment of almost zero and an acceptable storage claim
handoff: nothing further
input: the works cited
rhetorical job: none reusable
analytical job: record the mix of method papers, a handbook and a plan
output: twenty-three entries
handoff: none

main_argument_chains.claim: Recomputing the maximum flow at each time step gives an evacuation order and shows the bottlenecks.
support_steps: The linear speed and the stable speed supply the channel capacities.
Two virtual nodes reduce the building to one source and one sink.
The margin, maximum flow minus actual flow, flags the channels that limit the exit.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The staff widen the limiting channel and open extra exits near the far rooms.

main_argument_chains.claim: The same plan runs on the real building and clears it in about five minutes.
support_steps: The Louvre is reduced to five plane graphs linked by stairs.
The exit flow starts near 140 persons per second and falls to near zero by about 290 seconds.
A five percent density error moves the curves only at the final drop.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Responders are admitted late, once some channels have gone quiet.

warnings.warning: Equation (2) prints a minus on the left-hand side, so a positive damping force accelerates the person the prose says is slowed.
The paper says it substitutes an undefined quantity a into equation (1) to reach equation (5), which does not follow from equation (1).
rho is defined as rho_1 times rho_2 and set equal to D, but the product has units persons squared per square metre while D is persons per square metre.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Shows the source and sink nodes that reduce the building to one start and one end.
Shows how the four matrices occupy the overall matrix.
Gives the flow at three times that the prose reads as an ordered plan.
Contrasts exit flow with its margin to locate the supply shortfall.
Shows the Louvre flow at four times with the exits meeting at the sink.
Carries the five-minute claim as a curve ending near 290 seconds.
Marks fully loaded channels against spare ones so the route can be replanned.
Shows the five percent density error separating the curves only at the final drop.
